note: group systems is the closest of the five atlas groups (input–response with saturation); the page is biochemistry

description.zh: 酶像一把专配的锁钥：底物少时酶空闲着，速率随浓度涨；底物多了，酶分子全被占满，速率就饱和了——这就是米氏曲线的平台；温度与 pH 各有最适点，偏离则酶变形失活；抑制剂或抢位置（竞争性），或另找结合位点拖慢酶（非竞争性）。单底物稳态教学模型。
description.en: An enzyme fits its substrate like a lock and key: with little substrate most enzymes sit idle and the rate rises with concentration, but with plenty of substrate every enzyme is occupied and the rate saturates — the plateau of the Michaelis–Menten curve. Temperature and pH each have an optimum, away from which the enzyme deforms and fails; inhibitors either compete for the same spot (competitive) or bind elsewhere and slow the enzyme (non-competitive). A single-substrate steady-state teaching model.

reason.zh: 酶降低反应的活化能，使反应在体温下就能很快进行。
reason.en: An enzyme lowers a reaction's activation energy so it runs quickly at body temperature.

reason.zh: 速率随底物浓度先线性后饱和，是系统中常见的饱和非线性，抑制剂可被视为负反馈的一个分子实现。
reason.en: The rate rises linearly with substrate and then saturates, a common nonlinearity in systems, and inhibitors can act as a molecular form of negative feedback.

label.en: Slope and asymptote of a curve

reason.zh: 米氏曲线在 [S] = 0 处斜率为 Vmax/Kₘ，在大 [S] 处趋于水平的渐近线 Vmax。
reason.en: The Michaelis–Menten curve has slope Vmax/Kₘ at [S] = 0 and flattens toward the asymptote Vmax at large [S].

title.zh: 为什么酶也会“忙不过来”？
title.en: Why can an enzyme get "too busy"?

ask.zh: 酶降低活化能——底物浓度很低时，反应速率由什么限制？浓度高了呢？
ask.en: Enzymes lower the activation energy — at very low substrate concentration, what limits the rate? And at high concentration?

ask.zh: 米氏饱和曲线为什么会饱和？所有酶分子都被占满时，再加底物还有用吗？
ask.en: Why does the Michaelis–Menten curve level off? Once every enzyme is occupied, does adding more substrate help?

ask.zh: 产物积累会反过来抑制酶吗？这种反馈对细胞有什么好处？
ask.en: Can accumulating product feed back to slow the enzyme? What good does that feedback do the cell?

reveal.zh: 酶分子数量有限，底物多了酶全被占满，速率就饱和了；产物反馈抑制还能自动调节快慢。
reveal.en: Enzyme molecules are limited; with plenty of substrate they are all busy and the rate saturates; product feedback inhibition then regulates the pace automatically.
